ranked.headline: Fine-tuned sequence language models target antimicrobial peptides and resistance genes
ranked.summary: New preprints adapt ESM-2, ProGen and DNA language models to AMP design, AMR annotation and metagenomic taxonomy, alongside ML-augmented metabolic models.

ranked.headline: Benchmarks and calibration test where foundation models and inference tools hold up
ranked.summary: Preprints test protein and single-cell foundation models for leakage, baseline parity and error control, plus recalibrated pathway and kinase inference.

ranked.headline: Cancer transcriptome interpretation expands via chimeric RNA atlases and knowledgebases
ranked.summary: New NAR database releases and fusion/chimeric RNA tools refine reference layers for interpreting cancer transcriptomes and their regulators.

ranked.headline: Perturbation predictors face scrutiny of decoder limits, plate confounds and context transfer
ranked.summary: New preprints audit STATE's decoder, expose plate-layout confounds in screen benchmarks, and propose context-aware models for unseen perturbations.

ranked.headline: Molecular models predict cancer survival, drug response and immunotherapy toxicity
ranked.summary: New tools span methylation-based pediatric brain tumor prognostics, cell-line-to-tumour drug response transfer and scRNA-seq prediction of immune toxicity.

ranked.headline: Sequence foundation models are tested for hidden shortcuts such as ligand invariance and reading-frame reliance
ranked.summary: New preprints pair modality-specific pretraining with audits showing models ignoring ligand identity or relying on reading-frame cues absent from splicing machinery.

ranked.headline: Open-source pipelines quantify functional and morphological heterogeneity in iPSC-derived cells and organoids
ranked.summary: Three tools automate heterogeneity quantification in cardiomyocyte Ca2+ signals, patient-derived cell calcium traces and neural organoid morphology.

ranked.headline: Workflow-level benchmarks compare DIA search, quantification and downstream tools on spike-in and real data
ranked.summary: Five studies benchmark DIA workflows end to end, from search and quantification to plasma and cardiovascular applications, informing practical tool selection.

ranked.headline: Perturb-seq models shift toward causal, regulatory-path inference and flow-based response prediction
ranked.summary: New preprints pair perturbation response generation with causal GRN and regulatory-path inference from Perturb-seq, scATAC and lineage data.

ranked.headline: Integrated databases consolidate gut microbiome and gut disease omics data for reuse
ranked.summary: Two NAR database releases pool human gut microbiome and gut disease omics data, offering unified resources for cross-cohort and cross-disease analysis.

ranked.headline: Tools derive splicing events, annotation and isoform regulation from transcript-level RNA-seq
ranked.summary: New tools turn transcript sets and long-read data into splicing events, annotations and isoform atlases, while Ribo-seq and bacterial RNA-seq are repurposed for termini.

ranked.headline: Structural pocket, ligand and fold representations are repurposed for interaction and design prediction
ranked.summary: Fresh preprints and a BioLiP3 update extend structure-derived ligand, pocket and fold representations to fragment hits, DDI ranking, antibody screening and design.

ranked.headline: Discrete learned tokenizers and symmetry-aware encodings are being applied across DNA, RNA, protein and signal models
ranked.summary: Recent preprints tokenize structures, DNA and nanopore signal, while RNA models add structural guidance and stratified benchmarks for generalization.

ranked.headline: Unbalanced optimal transport and bridge models recover continuous dynamics from snapshot omics
ranked.summary: New preprints add lineage barcodes, chromatin coupling, spatial context and interpretable states to trajectory inference from static single-cell and spatial snapshots.

ranked.headline: Somatic variant calling shifts onto pangenome and germline-composite references, with long reads for SVs
ranked.summary: Three preprints and a published benchmark apply pangenome or composite germline references to somatic SV and variant detection, with long-read tumor-normal data.

ranked.headline: Compact physical and stochastic models describe protein backbone, B-factor and MD dynamics
ranked.summary: Three preprints propose reduced, physically structured models of protein fluctuations, with scaling gains for B-factors and MD reduction up to 738 dimensions.

ranked.headline: LLM agents move from design and planning toward autonomous lab execution, auditing, and red-teaming
ranked.summary: Agents now span antibody design, drug discovery, lab operations and model auditing, while biosecurity red-teaming and benchmarks test their reliability.

ranked.headline: Models reuse knowledge across cohorts and cancers, with scrutiny of baselines and calibration
ranked.summary: Preprints pair cross-cohort and cross-cancer transfer with tests against simple baselines, showing where added model complexity does or does not help.

ranked.headline: Sequence models extend variant effect prediction to methylation, single-molecule accessibility and 3D context
ranked.summary: Wreath, Mola and CellReg3D move sequence-based regulatory prediction toward methylation, single-molecule and cell-type-resolved targets.

ranked.headline: Moss genomes and zygnematophyte phylogenomics expand sampling at the base of land plants
ranked.summary: New moss assembly, U/V sex chromosome, and zygnematophyte transcriptome data broaden genomic coverage of early-diverging green lineages.

ranked.headline: Discovering functional DNA elements directly from nucleotide sequence
ranked.summary: Expanded plasmid metagenome catalogs and oriV annotations arrive alongside a motif-agnostic tool for TIGR array discovery from unannotated sequence.

ranked.headline: Computational methods assign spatial transcriptomic measurements to cells and states
ranked.summary: Current work separates cell abundance, intrinsic state, and neighbor spillover when attributing spatial transcriptomic measurements to cells.

ranked.headline: Genome-scale models and learned predictors map bacterial gene and metabolic function
ranked.summary: Bacterial genome mapping now spans metabolic models, interactomes, and proteome annotation, extending function assignment across strains and species.

ranked.headline: Installable upstream tools now standardize data preparation before statistical inference
ranked.summary: Preflight QC, reproducible dataset construction, and single-cell count processing are now released as standalone software steps ahead of analysis.

ranked.headline: Sequence-based recovery of gene-family members and coding content beyond annotation
ranked.summary: Annotation-independent assembly searches recover divergent and tandemly arrayed gene-family members, reportedly outperforming annotation-based methods.

ranked.headline: Histology and transcriptomics predict spatial protein and multi-omic profiles
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers infer spatial protein, expression and nuclear morphology from partial inputs, reducing reliance on dense paired measurements.

ranked.headline: Compact learned representations link genome sequence and structure to regulatory features
ranked.summary: Compact learned representations from sequence and contact maps are being tested for interpretable links to regulatory and structural genome features.

ranked.headline: Deep-learning RNA structure predictions are assessed against experimental references
ranked.summary: AlphaFold 3 accuracy drops on novel RNAs, driving validation and confidence scoring for RNA and protein-RNA predictions.

ranked.headline: Population-scale models resolve cell-type, isoform and sex-biased expression variation
ranked.summary: Large GTEx and single-cell cohorts now allow expression variation to be tested at population scale across tissues, cell types and sexes.

ranked.headline: De novo sequencing errors trace to limited fragment coverage in MS/MS
ranked.summary: Recent benchmarks and tools expose fragment-evidence limits in de novo sequencing while search and localization methods narrow ambiguity.

ranked.headline: Structured representations and pruning replace dense computation in sequence analysis
ranked.summary: Recent preprints report linear-time, multithreaded, and pangenome-scale methods that trade dense computation for pruned or structured alternatives.

ranked.headline: Polymer and generative models infer hidden rules of 3D genome folding and inheritance
ranked.summary: Recent preprints use polymer and generative models to infer cohesin kinetics and mitotic structural memory from chromosome folding data.

ranked.headline: Stochastic gene expression links fluctuating transcription to growth and state switching
ranked.summary: Exact stochastic simulation and growth-coupled noise models now test how fluctuating expression drives cell-state heterogeneity.

ranked.headline: Epigenetic, somatic and mobile-element variation mapped across plants and human tissues
ranked.summary: New methods now resolve somatic mutations, mobile element insertions and unmethylated regions in bulk and population-scale sequencing.

ranked.headline: Structure-based inference links disease variants to protein structural features
ranked.summary: Conserved hydration sites and interactome-wide interface modelling now connect missense pathogenicity to protein structure at scale.

ranked.headline: Algorithmic reformulations advance species tree inference and rooted tree partitioning
ranked.summary: Quantum annealing, million-taxon coalescent inference, and exact rooted-tree partitioning now make tree-level problems tractable at larger scales.

ranked.headline: Models prioritize regulatory variants across eQTL, GWAS, and fine-mapping contexts
ranked.summary: Recent methods prioritize noncoding variants via unsupervised scoring, LD-mismatch-robust fine-mapping, and causal network inference from trios.

ranked.headline: Stochastic and heterogeneous variation in disease and population models
ranked.summary: Recent work pairs agent- and subpopulation-level variation with formal attribution of stochastic noise in disease and population models.

ranked.headline: Dynamics-aware benchmarks test protein predictions beyond static structural accuracy
ranked.summary: Static success metrics for designed and predicted protein structures can overstate dynamical fidelity, motivating ensemble and MD-based assessment.

ranked.headline: Testing identifiability and assumptions behind transcriptomic inference models
ranked.summary: Expression-based inferences are being stress-tested for context dependence, component identifiability and cross-state coherence rather than fit alone.
